items.quote: The worker bee is one of the best-known symbols of Manchester.
Oasis are an English rock band formed in Manchester in 1991.
items.note: Easy: 'Gallagher brothers' plus 'Wonderwall' is two giveaways in one question. Fine for a family round; drop one clue if you want it to bite.

items.quote: Coronation Street (colloquially referred to as Corrie) is a British television soap opera created by Granada Television and shown on ITV since 9 December 1960.
items.note: Same article: 'The programme centres on a cobbled, terraced street in the fictional town of Weatherfield in Greater Manchester.'

items.quote: Cottonopolis was a 19th-century nickname for Manchester, as it was a metropolis and the centre of the cotton industry.
items.note: Nitpick: the article says the nickname was acquired in the early 19th century, i.e. before Victoria; '19th-century Manchester' would be exact. Answer unaffected.

items.quote: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway (L&MR) was the first inter-city railway in the world.
Factory Records was a Manchester-based British independent record label founded in 1978 by Tony Wilson and Alan Erasmus.
The Peterloo Massacre took place at St Peter's Field, Manchester, England, on Monday 16 August 1819.
items.note: Mild giveaway: 'St Peter's Field' is where the 'Peter' in Peterloo comes from. Acceptable; say 'in central Manchester' instead if you want it harder.

items.quote: In 1903, Pankhurst founded the Women's Social and Political Union (WSPU), an all-women suffrage advocacy organisation
items.note: Same article: 'Rise up, Women, a statue of Pankhurst in St Peter's Square in Manchester, her home town' (unveiled 14 December 2018). Her daughters helped found the WSPU, but the statue clause pins it to Emmeline.

items.quote: The Alan Turing Memorial, situated in Sackville Gardens in Manchester, England, is a sculpture in memory of Alan Turing, a pioneer of modern computing.
Built to host the 2002 Commonwealth Games, the stadium has since staged the 2008 UEFA Cup final
items.note: The article adds that it was first proposed as an athletics arena for Manchester's failed 2000 Olympics bid, so a pedant may say 'the Olympics'; 'built for' makes the Commonwealth Games correct. Ground is now the Etihad Stadium; Man City moved in 2003.
